summary:
For the cheapest main, find the dearest side that still fits; every cheaper side fits too. As mains get
pricier, that boundary can only move toward cheaper sides, so one pointer sweeping down the sides handles all
mains: O(n + m). The count can exceed 2³¹, so use 64 bits.

question.md:
Count (main, side) pairs with `main + side ≤ budget`. Both price lists are sorted.

- **Up to 10⁵ of each**: up to 10¹⁰ pairs, so the count needs 64 bits.
- Prices up to 10⁹: sums up to 2 × 10⁹, use 64-bit sums.

think.md:
Mains `[5, 8, 12, 20]`, sides `[2, 4, 9, 11]`, budget 16: **8** pairs fit.

For a fixed main, the sides that fit form a prefix of the sorted sides (all prices up to `budget − main`).
The prefix length is what we add. And when the main gets more expensive, the allowed prefix can only shrink, so
the boundary pointer never needs to move back.

idea.md: Count every pair whose total is within budget.

lines.text: Every pair, with a 64-bit sum and count.

limits.md: Up to 10¹⁰ pairs. The fitting sides form a prefix, so we can count them without visiting them.

idea.md: For each main `x`, count sides `≤ budget − x` with an upper-bound binary search.

lines.text: The number of sides that cost at most `budget − x`: the first index with a bigger price.

walk.title: For each main, binary-search how many sides cost at most budget − main.

limits.md: Each search restarts, even though the boundary only moves one way as mains grow. A single sweeping pointer makes it linear.

idea.md: `j` starts at the dearest side. For each main from cheapest to dearest, move `j` left while `main + sides[j] > budget`; add `j + 1`.

lines.text: Count, and `j` on the dearest side.
Drop sides that no longer fit with this (or any pricier) main.

complexity.md: **Time O(n + m):** `j` only moves left. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: Main 5: the pointer settles on side 11, so 4 side(s) fit.
Main 8: the pointer settles on side 4, so 2 side(s) fit.
Main 12: the pointer settles on side 4, so 2 side(s) fit.
Main 20: the pointer settles on nothing, so 0 side(s) fit.

walk.title: Cheapest main first, with a pointer on the dearest side that still fits. As mains get pricier, the pointer only moves left.

takeaways.md:
- **Counting pairs under a bound across two sorted lists:** one pointer per list, moving monotonically.
- When a boundary only moves one way, a sweep beats repeated binary searches.
- Counts of pairs can exceed 32 bits.
